EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows (a) strong C–H stretches at 2890-2990 cm⁻¹, (b) a single intense C=O stretch at 1733 cm⁻¹ characteristic of a saturated aliphatic ester carbonyl, (c) a CH₃/CH bending band at 1458 cm⁻¹, and (d) several C–O/ C–C–O stretches for esters in the 1080-1180 cm⁻¹ and 830-930 cm⁻¹ regions. No bands appear near 1650 cm⁻¹ (amide C=O) or 2250 cm⁻¹ (N=C=O), excluding candidates 5 and 8; the required carbonyl band rules out ether (3) and carbonyl-free species (6, 10). Among the remaining esters (1, 2, 4), candidate 1 (isopropyl acetate, CCC(=O)OC(C)C) best matches the prominent ~830/876/927 cm⁻¹ doublet–triplet pattern of isopropyl esters and lacks CH₂ groups (consistent with a single 1458 cm⁻¹ CH₃ bend and no separate CH₂ scissoring near 1470 cm⁻¹). Therefore candidate 1 provides the most coherent fit to the observed Raman peaks.
